welcome.title: Welcome aboard
welcome.body:
I'm HT — Hilmi Tolga Şahin. By day I lead engineering teams at IKEA in Amsterdam. By night I build small things: games for my kids, AI that runs on your own device, and odd little toys for the web.

Make yourself at home. Open the chest and slot a cartridge into the handheld to play. The chart on the table shows the voyage so far. And if you'd like to say hi, the message bottle will carry a note to me.

about.title: The captain
about.body:
I'm HT. Curious, engineer, maker, mathematician — in that order.

I've been on GitHub since 2011 and leading teams since 2014. Today I'm an engineering manager at IKEA (Ingka) in Amsterdam: three teams and ten direct reports on the global supply-chain planning platform. The ports before that are on the chart.

I like async work, docs as artefacts and meeting-free Fridays, and I'd rather cut 80% than add more. Off duty it's games (Godot, three.js, tabletop RPGs), Tolkien and Tengwar, aviation, Nostr, and AI that runs on your own device.

Küçük kanat means “little wing”.

story.body:
My father was ex-military and, in his spare time, a bit of a mad scientist. One night he woke me at 2 AM with a question: what is the square root of minus one?

It's a strange thing to ask a sleepy kid. No ordinary number squares to minus one. So mathematicians gave it a name, i, and a whole new world of numbers opened up.

That question stayed with me. Maths is the root of my love of software: start from something solid, and you can build almost anything on it.

Life is too short for hype-hopping. Build a foundation.

items.title: Fast Is Not Enough
items.subtitle: What AI does to team size and delivery
items.body:
My research on what AI really does to team size and delivery time. Writing code faster is one thing; delivering faster is another.

I spoke about it at ACCELER8IT in Gdańsk in 2026.

items.title: ALE Manifesto
items.subtitle: Accessible · Living · Easy to contribute
items.body:
I wrote this in 2016: three rules for documentation people actually use. Keep it accessible, keep it living, make it easy to add to.

An outdated chart is worse than no chart at all.

items.title: bots
items.subtitle: Plush avatars for AI agents
items.label: /labels/bots.webp
items.body: Fourteen plush shapes and nine creatures that look around, hop while they work and doze off between tasks. Tell one what your agent is doing and it works out the rest. Think of them as the crew's mascots.

items.title: edgewise
items.subtitle: Six verbs for on-device AI
items.label: /labels/edgewise.webp
items.body: Language, vision, speech, judging, embedding, image and forecasting models that run where your code runs: in the browser through WebGPU or WebAssembly, and in Bun or Node through ONNX Runtime. No server in the loop.

items.title: Tilt Town
items.subtitle: Painterly city builder
items.label: /labels/tilttown.webp
items.body:
Build a crooked, Porto-style riverside town of leaning houses and red roofs, then watch its people live in it.

Citizens with daily plans, an economy and requests; faces that blink, smile and talk up close; day and night, weather and seasons.

items.title: INKWAKE
items.subtitle: Issue #1: The Unprinted Wood
items.label: /labels/inkwake.webp
items.body:
A pulp comic that hasn't been printed yet. Your crystal sheds ink, not light: wherever it shines, the page gets drawn.

Four heroes, three pages and a boss called THE EDITOR, in five to eight minutes.

items.title: Liquid Glass
items.subtitle: Real refraction for the web
items.label: /labels/liquid-glass.webp
items.body: React components whose edges really bend the light behind them, built on SVG displacement maps. Like looking through old cabin glass.

items.title: speech
items.subtitle: Voice cloning in the browser
items.label: /labels/speech.webp
items.body: Voice-cloning text-to-speech and streaming speech-to-text, on your own device, in the browser. No server, no API key.

items.title: Bunker
items.subtitle: Your own private app cloud
items.label: /labels/bunker.webp
items.body: Drop in a file or folder, or describe an app in plain words, and get a private web app you can share with a link. One Go binary, one data folder. A small hold for your own things.

items.labelPrompt: A cosy family Christmas tabletop game night seen from above: a warm wooden table with a small painted game board of a snowy village, two chunky white six-sided dice with clear black pips mid-roll, tiny hero figurines, a glowing gold star, candlelight and pine branches with red berries around the edge. Warm, bright, festive.
items.title: Hearthside
items.subtitle: The family Christmas RPG
items.label: /labels/hearthside.webp
items.body:
Sleighbound: get the stolen Star back before midnight.

I built this co-op tabletop RPG so I could be game master for my two kids at Christmas. A 3D table, flick-to-throw dice, and everyone plays on their own phone over encrypted Nostr relays.

items.title: tiny
items.subtitle: A minimal PWA chat client
items.label: /labels/tiny.webp
items.body: A minimal chat client for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Plugins ship in the build or install at runtime.

items.title: Beambox
items.subtitle: A microVM for every agent
items.label: /labels/beambox.webp
items.body: A desktop app and CLI that give each AI agent its own sandboxed computer, a microVM of its own. The agent can make a mess in there instead of on your deck.

items.title: game0
items.subtitle: A sky-island MMORPG, in concept
items.label: /labels/game0.webp
items.body:
Floating isles, winds, ships and peoples. A world bible first, a game later. You may recognise the skies outside this window.

The handbook already has playable mini demos.

items.title: Routers
items.subtitle: Zero-shot prompt routing
items.label: /labels/lfm-encoders.webp
items.body: Zero-shot prompt routing, policy linting and masked-diffusion text generation. All of it runs in your browser, nothing leaves port.

items.title: js13k
items.subtitle: A game in 13 kilobytes
items.label: /labels/js13k.webp
items.body: My first game jam, in 2018: a tiny engine and a game that had to fit in 13 KB. Good practice in packing light.

items.title: LocalDB
items.subtitle: MongoDB in the browser
items.label: /labels/localdb.webp
items.body: A tiny document database on top of localStorage, from 2015. My oldest hit.

items.title: Dice Roller
items.subtitle: RPG dice in Godot
items.label: /labels/dice.webp
items.body: A simple RPG dice roller. Mostly my excuse to learn Godot.

items.labelPrompt: A friendly purple ostrich with a long neck, long bare legs and fluffy black-and-white plumage, clearly an ostrich, wearing a small graduation cap, standing at a chalkboard covered in glowing connected dots like a network of relays, a cosy classroom, bright and cheerful.
items.title: Nostr School
items.subtitle: An explorable Nostr course
items.label: /labels/nostrschool.webp
items.body: Learn the Nostr protocol by poking at it. I like protocols nobody owns.

items.title: How to work with me
items.subtitle: My user manual
items.body:
My user manual. If it's not documented, it doesn't exist.

Async first, links over “hello”, meeting-free Fridays. Ask me anything — literally anything.
